keyVerseText: And he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun אֶשְׁפָּר (ʼeshpâr) is of uncertain derivation, with no clear root word identified. Its core sense, as reflected in the Strong's and lexicon definitions, centers on a 'good piece' or a measured portion of flesh or food. This literal sense of a carefully allotted or valued portion goes beyond a simple English translation, suggesting something set apart and given with intention and care.
usageInScripture: The word אֶשְׁפָּר occurs only twice in Scripture, consistently translated as 'a good piece' or 'a good piece of flesh.' This limited usage highlights a specific context of distribution or sharing of food among people, emphasizing both the physical sustenance and the measured generosity involved. The consistency in translation underscores its meaning as a tangible, valued portion rather than a generic piece of meat or cake.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֶשְׁפָּר as a measured, good portion enriches our appreciation of God's provision and the communal sharing evident in biblical narratives. It reflects the care and intentionality in giving, reminding believers that God’s blessings are not arbitrary but thoughtfully allotted. This word invites reflection on the goodness and sufficiency of what God provides, encouraging gratitude and trust in His faithful provision. It also points to the unity and fellowship fostered when God's people share generously with one another.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 6:19, where it says, 'And he dealt among all the people... a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine,' the term אֶשְׁפָּר highlights the generous and measured distribution of sustenance to the people. This 'good piece' conveys not just quantity but quality and care, illustrating the joy and abundance accompanying David’s celebration. It reminds us that God's blessings are both plentiful and purposefully shared among His people.
